Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Global Wealth Partners Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the question and answer session, please press star one if you would like to register a question. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Wealth Partners's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; Robert Kline, Head of Distribution; Elena Vasquez, Head of Operations; Mark Forrester, Head of Risk Management; and Nina Patel, Head of Technology.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust AUM growth and a favorable geographic breakdown that highlights our global diversification. Our AUM grew to $785 billion.

As we dive into our results, I'd like to start with our core franchise metric: assets under management, or AUM. We delivered another quarter of strong growth, reaching a record $785 billion as of September 30th, up 14% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This underscores the resilience of our diversified platform amid volatility, including the Fed's 50-basis-point rate cut signaling a potential soft landing, persistent inflation in Europe, and China's stimulus boosting regional equities.

Total expansion came from strong long-term net inflows of $18.2 billion—our highest since Q1 2022—plus market appreciation of $22.4 billion, offset slightly by $1.1 billion outflows in lower-margin cash equivalents as clients shifted to higher-yielding fixed income and alternatives. Organic growth, excluding markets and FX, was 8% YoY, reflecting focus on high-conviction strategies like active equity SMAs and model portfolios.

Geographically, our global footprint stands out: North America at 53% or $416 billion; Europe 26% or $204 billion; Asia-Pacific 16% or $126 billion; Rest of World 5% or $39 billion. Compared to last year—North America 56%, Europe 24%, Asia 14%, ROW 6%—we've rebalanced toward emerging markets.

In North America, 53% of AUM at $416 billion with 11% YoY growth, inflows hit $10.5 billion. Retail and RIA drove 60%, DC plans like 401(k)s and IRAs 25%, amid S&P 500 up 22% YTD. Our GWP Core Equity ETF (GWPQ), blending large-cap growth/value with ESG at 0.08% expense ratio, saw $4.2 billion inflows, beating iShares Core S&P 500 with active overlays. Institutions added $2.8 billion via wirehouses like Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch using our Aladdin-like analytics for SMAs. We countered fee compression by upselling alternatives—private credit interval fund up 25% YoY to $15B. We're expanding retirement tech with Fidelity and Schwab robo integrations for the $30 trillion market.

Europe, 26% or $204B, up 16% YoY, had $5.1 billion inflows from sustainable investing and ECB dovishness. UCITS ETFs shone, GWP Euro Sustainable Equity ETF tracking MSCI Europe SRI pulling €3.2 billion under SFDR Article 8/9. UK/Nordics pensions added $2.1 billion to multi-asset target-date funds with VaR models. Continental gains from DWS/Amundi platforms with passive+ hybrids amid MiFID II. Organic up 12% plus FX tailwinds. Seeded €500 million into pan-European private markets fund-of-funds for infrastructure/real assets in EU green transition. Despite French elections, our 15% ESG AUM share leads peers like Legal & General.

Asia-Pacific, 16% or $126B, up 28% YoY, saw $2.4 billion inflows, 10th straight accelerating quarter. Japan/China 55%: GPIF into J-REIT/yen-hedged ETFs ($1.7B) on BOJ normalization. China/SE Asia $900 million on wealth transfer—super-rich doubling to 1M by 2030 per UBS. Hong Kong/Singapore Cross-Border Wealth Connect like Vanguard Asia ex-Japan but with A-shares, $600M Day 1. India $400M in EM debt. Invested $50M in APAC data infra with AI sentiment from Baidu/Tencent. Targeting 20% total AUM from Asia by 2026 via JVs like BlackRock-ChinaAMC, ring-fencing onshore/offshore.

Rest of World, 5% or $39B, up 9% YoY, $200M inflows led by Middle East SWFs—ADIA/PIF $1.2B YTD to global macro hedge at 12% NAV on oil rebound. LatAm via Brazil pensions $150M in equity SMA. Higher 45 bps fees vs 28 bps global boost margins.

Forward, expect $850B year-end on 5-7% markets, $15-20B quarterly inflows. $1B to tokenization pilots with Ripple/State Street for PE/RE blockchain. Counter 32 bps fee compression (down from 35) with 20% fee-based alts up 30% YoY. Risks: US election, China property; but 60/40 mix, 47% ex-NA, Sharpe 1.2 top-quartile. This validates our global alpha, local beta playbook.

David Chen: Thank you, Michael. From a financial perspective, Global Wealth Partners delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $2.1 billion, representing a 15% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by our mergers and acquisitions activity, a key pillar of inorganic growth amid industry fee compression—down 15 bps YoY on active equity per Morningstar—and shifts to passive/alternatives with ETF AUM over $12T globally. Disciplined M&A scales us, diversifies, captures alpha in private credit/ESG.

We closed two transformative deals, third in exclusivity. First, acquired Horizon Alternative Strategies, London boutique in direct lending/opportunistic credit, $1.2B deal (60% cash, 40% SOFR+125bps loan), adds $28B AUM to alts now >$150B up 22% QoQ. Horizon's 14% IRR past 5 years fits private credit push amid ECB hawkishness/Europe banking fragmentation. $85M run-rate synergies Year 2 from back-office/Aladdin risk, OpEx/AUM from 45bps to <30bps. 12% accretive to adj EPS, 18% pro forma ROIC >12% hurdle.

Bolsters EMEA alts inflows up 35% YoY from pensions amid UK gilts/German Bunds at 2.8%. Cross-sell to $400B inst SA book for 200bps fee uplift.

Second, merger of equals with Pacific Wealth Advisors, SF RIA $42B AUM in HNW sustainable equity. $2.8B all-stock at 0.85x FY24 rev, like Fisher to KKR. Integrates top-quartile ESG ETFs, $6.2B YTD inflows on S&P ESG +250bps. Q1 FY25 close, $120M ann synergies from OMS/distribution via Schwab/Fidelity. 8% EPS accretive Year 1, 15% ann AUM CAGR from RIA flows.

Addresses RIA fee drag (55% distribution mix up from 40%), captures $80T wealth transfer per Cerulli. Launched co-branded UCITS ETFs in Europe on SFDR demand, ESG AUM up 28% YoY.

Ahead, $5B dry powder from $1.1B Q3 FCF targets APAC quant/infra debt at 25% CAGR per Preqin. NDAs on three, incl Singapore GP stakes for $90B portfolio amid LP co-invests. 40+ leads via IR/Goldman/Evercore.

These add $70B net new AUM YTD, fortify 45bps fee vs beta erosion. Entering consolidation like State Street/Amundi; our 2x TSR since 2020 shows discipline.

Our expenses were $1.4 billion, resulting in net income of $550 million. Our expense ratio improved due to synergies from these deals.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities. We are navigating the current market environment by delivering strong total net flows of $18.7 billion for the quarter ended September 30th, up 24% YoY from $15.1 billion in Q3 last year and accelerating from $14.2 billion in Q2. Six-month cumulative $32.9 billion, 4.2% organic growth ex-markets/FX.

By asset class: Equities $9.4B inflows up 35% QoQ, passive/smart-beta; GWP S&P 500 ETF suite $45B AUM took $4.2B on equity rally/AI. Active equities $2.8B, EM ex-China $1.1B for India/SE Asia alpha.

Fixed income $5.6B up 18%, rotation to duration on Fed cuts; short-duration/IG corps $3.1B, money markets 5.25% yield $1.8B from deposits. Minimal outflows longer core-plus.

Alts/multi-asset $3.1B, private credit $1.9B incl $750M European pension to direct lending. Evergreen target-date $900M retail.

Modest $400M outflows commodities/cash.

By channel: Institutional $11.2B (60%) up 42% YoY, three SWF mandates $4.5B—EMEA ESG equities, APAC infra debt. Intermediary/retail $5.3B, wealth mgrs $2.2B via SMA on Envestnet/SEI.

Regions: Americas $12.1B (65%) on 401(k)/DCIO $1.2B RFP top-10 provider. EMEA $4.3B UCITS/MiFID/SFDR. APAC $2.3B up 15% QoQ HK/SG HNW Asia ex-China.

Trends: wealth transfer, ETF adoption (55% equity AUM), flight to quality geopolitics. Flows Optimizer AI flagged segments, 28% conversion up 300bps.

Framework: scale passives $320B ETFs; differentiate alts 85bps fees to $100B FY26; embed ESG/tech, carbon-alpha 40% AUM post-COP28, tokenization pilots BlackRock/Franklin.

Expect Q4 $16-20B flows on $45B pipeline, SIP, Bitcoin ETP Europe. Risks high rates, but 65/35 bias/$150B liquidity.

We launched our new AI & Digital Innovation ETF this quarter, and early reception positive with strong inflows.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our equity funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific are paying off, as evidenced by our technology and digital platform investments. In this industry with intensifying fee compression, regulatory scrutiny, and client demands for transparency/personalization, tech is our moat. $450M tech capex past 12 months, 8% opex up from 6%, 25-30% 3-yr ROI on retention/efficiencies/revenue.

Next-gen digital platform Q2 rollout on AWS microservices integrates Bloomberg/FactSet. Usage up 65% YoY to 1.2M logins. Inst ESG dashboards SFDR/TCFD cut recon 40%; retail robo $18B AUM up 120%, $250M/mo inflows, hybrid AI 15-20bps better vs Vanguard/Betterment.

AI/data: $120M AlphaForge GenAI PMS, NLP 10k alt data (satellites/social), ETF liquidity predict. Q3 12% slippage improvement, $35M TC savings. Quantum opto fixed income IBM, 8-10% duration efficiency.

Regions: APAC 72% digital, WeChat mini-app 45% HNW AUM China/SE Asia vs Hillhouse. Europe MiFID algo trading +30% post-Brexit. Americas Charles River to 92% STP from 78%.

Digital 28% net flows up from 15%, $85M platform fees +55%. Q4 blockchain admin DTCC/State Street RWA tokenization priv credit $16T TAM BCG, on-chain ESG vs BlackRock BUIDL.

FY25 $500M capex cyber/edge amid 25% attacks IBM. De-risks vs 42bps fees Morningstar, captures $10T passive/smart beta.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. Operationally, we've made significant progress in streamlining our middle and back office functions. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on management's outlook for AUM growth. We manage $785B quarter-end, +14% YoY +4.2% QoQ on markets/inflows.

Q3 $18.2B inflows >$15B guide, strongest since Q4 2021: $9.8B passive equity S&P/Nasdaq on AI/tech; $5.4B alts priv credit/infra on yields. Markets +$22B: equities 7.1%, FI 2.8% Fed cut, alts illiquids.

FY24 10-12% growth to $850-870B YE on 6-8% eq, 3-4% bonds. Organic $65-75B FY24 to $80-90B FY25; 15-20% ETF CAGR to $250B 2026, incl AI Innovators ETF (APAI) $1.2B seed July NVIDIA surge.

Markets/FX 40-50%, beta 0.85 <0.95 indy resilient vol. Inorganic 5-10bps tuck-ins like €ESG mgr $12B.

Regions: Americas 62% $486B growth engine US retirement $12B/q vs Vanguard. Apex Wealth robo 2.5M clients RIAs/wirehouses. EMEA 24% $188B 8-10% UCITS/target-date vs MiFID. APAC 14% $109B 18-22% China ETF/SG/HK $2B seed Asia ex-Japan "China+1" GIC/Temasek.

Pillars vs 28bps fees PwC/passive debate: 1) Innovation: Q4 interval priv credit 9-11% mid-mkt (Ares), RE debt data centers (Blackstone), ESG HY ETF SFDR; to 34bps blended 2026. 2) Tech/dist: Aligned Alpha ML tracking -15%, $150M blockchain Fidelity tokenized MM mid-2025 $10T Citi, millennial HNW. 3) Client scale: 65% inst up 58%, CalPERS $10B infra, OMERS PE, retail direct index $15B tax-alpha Parametric.

Risks: election eq 4-5%, infl>2.5% FI, regs priv funds SEC/AIFMD 10-15% slow, FX EMEA; hedge 70% USD. Conviction top-quartile vs T Rowe/Franklin, $1.5T 2030 12-15% CAGR ROE 18-20% no BlackRock M&A bloat.

Mark Forrester: Thank you, Elena. From a risk management perspective, we continue to maintain a robust framework to identify, assess, and mitigate risks across the organization. We have enhanced our monitoring of market volatility and are taking steps to address potential vulnerabilities. This includes the impact of market performance and net flows on AUM. For Q3 ended Sept 30, AUM hit record $1.28T? Wait, aligning to $785B scale, but dynamics similar: up 11% QoQ 22% YoY, 12th straight quarter on markets + net flows.

Avg daily $770B, fee rev $1.8B at 92bps? Adjusted to our 45bps blended up 14% YoY mix shift active.

Markets +$98B? Scaled: say +$60B (9.2% contrib). Equities $416B franchise +$28B S&P 9.2% MSCI ex-US 7.8% cooling infl/Fed pivot; US large active +210bps $20B. FI $204B +$12B Bloomy Agg 2.9% Treas 4.3-3.9%; short/IG strong, EM debt -1.2% China drag. Alts/multi $126B +$12B priv mkt 5.5% realizations Burgiss/Preqin conservative. FX -$1B euro weaken.

Net flows +$32B? Scaled $20B second-best ex $10B ETF seed, 15.6% ann organic >5-7% indy Morningstar.

Inst +$12B DC/SWF post-bank crisis. Retail/inter +$8B wirehouses ETFs. ETFs $15B +40% QoQ S&P ESG $8B 12bps clean energy $50B trend ETFGI. Active eq $6B 4-star Global Dividend. FI +$3B off $2B duration outflows.

Regions: NA 65% $13B, Europe 25% $6.5B UCITS MiFID, APAC 10% $2B HK feeders China rebound. Retention 97.5% CalPERS/Norges.

Reconc: start $710B +$60B mkt +$20B flows -$1B FX +$2B sales? = $785B end. Stablecoin/crypto $8B high margin >5%.

Initiatives: 1) Tech Aladdin GenAI op costs -15% active +50bps $20T passive-smart shift. 2) 5 new active ETFs Q4 $10B flows 130/30 MSCI ACWI. 3) APAC SG hub 20% flows 2025 ESG 28% up 18% YoY SFDR.

Q4 8-10% growth S&P flat+5% flows $20-25B; diversified 45% eq 25% FI 20% alts 10% cash vs pure eq peers.

Nina Patel: Thank you, Mark. On the technology front, we are investing in advanced analytics and AI to enhance our investment decision-making process and improve client service. We are also focused on strengthening our cybersecurity posture. Specifically, new product launches and fund performance rankings show strength. We've innovated for thematic/sustainable/alts amid inflation/geopolitics/AI boom.

Q3 launches three products $2.8B inflows first 45 days 35% beat. Apex AI & Digital Innovation ETF (AIDIX) smart-beta 150 AI/cloud/cyber leaders, factors fwd P/E/rev/ESG data ctr eff, 0.25% ER $1.2B AUM retail Schwab/Fid inst DC, +18% incp May15 outpace Nasdaq +450bps NVDA/ASML/CrowdStrike.

Apex Sustainable Transition Credit semi-liq interval $500M YE target priv credit energy trans green bonds/renew/project fin cleantech, Libor+550 ~9.2% net, HNW/RIAs post-zero rates $850M comm $200M EU pension SFDR8.

Apex EM Multi-Asset ETF (EMMAX) China+1 eq/LC bonds/commod ASEAN/LatAm 0.38% TER $750M APAC wirehouses yen unwind.

NextGen: $45M tech quant ML alt data sat/NLP transcripts Refinitiv ESG AWS backtest. Regions NA 55% Europe 25% MiFID APAC 20% SG hub SWF.

Global Sustainable Equity (GSEFX) 5-star 22.1% 1yr top decile large growth, under fossil over wind/solar Orsted/Enphase.

FI Short Duration HY (SDHYX) #3 Lipper 8.9% SOFR+420 spreads 475-380bps.

Alts Private Real Assets 12.5% net IRR top Preqin indus logis data ctrs.

12% organic YTD to 1.5% share 2025.

Michael Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes our capital allocation strategy. AUM $785B up12% YoY $28B? Scaled inflows ETF/alts. Framework three pillars: shareholder returns first, organic growth, inorganic. FCF robust $620M 9mo $850M ann 42% margin 150bps fees scalable.

Fortress BS $1.2B net cash IG <1x lev.

Shareholder 55-65% FCF: $380M YTD 61%, div +15% $0.45/q 2.8% yield. Buybacks 4.2M sh $92 avg 8% below IV +250bps EPS, $500M auth 70% YE <14x PE. 13% BVPS CAGR >T Rowe.

Organic 20-25% FCF $140M YTD +25%: Digital HorizonOne robo B2B $60M 35% retail AUM $180B direct index 15% marg APAC DBS $4B inflows. AI AlphaForge $50M alt data +220bps alpha Sharpe>1.5 vs RenTech $320B active eq. Alts infra $30M seed $5B priv credit 12% IRR ESG NetZero SFDR $12B EU.

Regions NA60% $870B? Scaled, APAC18% $260B +22% China/India, EMEA22% $320B UK LDI.

Inorganic 10-15% +tuck $80M seed 6 boutiques two launched $2B health PE 18% IRR timber 11% infl prot. Closed EuroVest $450M $45B AUM 8x FRE 300bps acc. Pipeline US midcap/Asia FI cash/ATM.

Trends: ETF 45% flows $1.2T YTD 2.5% share; alts $17T +15% Preqin 22% organic. Fees 58bps stab active/priv85bps. Risks election/infl hedge beta.

Ahead 60%+ FCF flex $900M+ 2025 $1.6T AUM. ROIC>17% special div/buybacks. 220% TSR since IPO >MSCI90%, sustain consolidation.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the drivers behind your AUM growth this quarter?

Michael Reynolds: Thanks, John. As Michael outlined earlier, our AUM hit $785 billion through strong inflows, market gains, and geographic balance—North America bedrock at $416 billion, Europe accelerating to $204 billion on ESG, Asia engine at $126 billion with Japan and China leading, and ROW high-margin. Organic 8% YoY, with forward to $850 billion on continued momentum.

John Smith: Thank you. And a follow-up on your M&A pipeline?

David Chen: John, our two Q3 closes added $70 billion AUM, accretive immediately, with $5 billion dry powder for APAC and quant tuck-ins. Robust 40 leads, disciplined at 15-20% IRR.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jane Doe with Morgan Stanley.

Jane Doe: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of GWP Core Equity ETF?

Lisa Patel: Absolutely, Jane. GWPQ saw $4.2 billion inflows, outperforming peers on low 0.08% fees and tactical overlays amid S&P gains. Part of our top-quartile strategies.

Jane Doe: And how is the new product AIDIX performing relative to expectations?

Robert Kline: Exceeding, Jane—$1.2 billion AUM already, 18% return since inception outpacing Nasdaq by 450 bps on AI leaders like NVIDIA.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan.

Mike Johnson: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

Elena Vasquez: Sure, Mike. Streamlining middle/back office via tech like AlphaForge has cut costs 15%, boosted retention to 92%, supporting our AUM outlook to $900 billion by 2025 through innovation and scale.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays.

Emily Chen: What are your thoughts on the current regulatory environment and its impact on your risk profile?

Mark Forrester: Emily, our robust framework monitors SFDR, MiFID, SEC priv fund rules closely. Diversified mix and conservative marking keep risks mitigated, with strong flows despite headwinds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Citi.

Tom Rivera: How are you leveraging technology to improve investment performance?

Nina Patel: Tom, AlphaForge AI with alt data and NLP improves slippage 12%, alpha +220 bps in sys eq. Digital platform drives 28% flows, positioning for tokenization.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Michael Reynolds for closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Global Wealth Partners. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
